claims.text: The powder feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
In situ monitoring of chemical short-range order during additive manufacturing can improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
Real-time SRO monitoring enables optimization of additive-manufacturing process parameters.
Process optimization based on SRO monitoring minimizes compositional segregation.
Process optimization based on SRO monitoring minimizes residual stress.
Process optimization based on SRO monitoring minimizes defect formation.
SRO-monitored additive manufacturing increases AlCrFeNiSi strength relative to conventional fabrication.
SRO-monitored additive manufacturing increases AlCrFeNiSi toughness relative to conventional fabrication.
SRO-monitored additive manufacturing reduces segregation relative to conventional fabrication.
SRO-monitored additive manufacturing reduces residual stress relative to conventional fabrication.
SRO-monitored additive manufacturing reduces defect formation relative to conventional fabrication.
The hypothesis is proposed to apply at processing temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The hypothesis is proposed to apply at printing speeds up to 1000 mm/s.
The hypothesis is proposed to apply when post-processing includes heat treatment or machining.
The relationship between SRO and mechanical properties is not yet fully understood.
Optimal process parameters for the proposed SRO-monitoring approach remain undetermined.

contradictions.description: The experimental design identifies additively manufactured material without SRO monitoring as the comparator, whereas the baseline and falsification rule use conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi. These are not necessarily the same control, leaving the decisive comparison inconsistent.
